FIX BUG #380: A secret a model echoes survives in its harness's own session file, and brokkr transcript, the TUI and the browser render it unmasked

You are fixing exactly one bug from the code-health epic (#330) on branch fix-380-transcript-masking, already checked out in this worktree, STACKED on branch fix-370-371-secrets-audience (PR #381, not yet merged), because this fix builds on #370's delivery and masking (bind_environment, secret::mask_json). Your diff is judged against that branch's head, not against main. The issue text is below and is the whole framing: its "Fix" and "Acceptance" sections are what done means. Where the issue says the operator rules between options, implement option 1 of the issue (mask at read time), and state on the surface when the store no longer holds a declared name, keep it small, and say in your result notes which option you took so the pull request can ask for the ruling.

RULES
- Scope: fix this bug and nothing beside it. Follow-ups go in your notes, not in the diff. Prefer targeted edits over rewrites.
- Tests: add or extend the suite that proves the fix. Assert exact values and exact error variants or text, never is_err() alone. Show every new test binds: make a compiling mutation that removes the fix, run the test and see it fail, restore the fix, and record the failing test name in your notes.
- Coverage: the repository enforces literal 100% line, branch and function coverage (scripts/coverage-exact.sh), which the controller runs after you; do not run that script. Keep every new line and branch reachable by a test. If a branch cannot be reached deterministically, restructure rather than leave it uncovered.
- Frozen surfaces do not move: contracts/, policy/phase-machine.json, fixtures/, reference/. Decisions 0001 and 0003 stand. Hosts are Linux and macOS only (decision 0063): add no Windows code.
- Every witness digest your change moves is re-pinned from the tests' own reported values, never computed by hand.
- Gates before you report complete, all clean: cargo fmt --all -- --check; cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings; cargo test for every crate you touched (crate-scoped: cargo test -p <crate>); git diff --check.
- Commit when done: one commit, signed off (git commit -s), message "<area>: <what changed> (#380)" in the repository's style, ending with the line "Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>". Never push.
- Evidence: every claim in your notes points to a command you ran in this session and what it printed. Anything you did not observe is pending, not done.

THE ISSUE (#380), verbatim:

Follow-up to #370, found while fixing it. Part of the code-health epic #330.

## What happens

Since #370, a secret a seat declares reaches its claude, codex or dsh harness through the child's environment, as decisions 0021 ruling 4 and 0036 ruling 4 intend. Brokkr masks every surface it journals: stderr, checkpoints, a provider's refusal and the result file.

**The harness's own session file is not one of those surfaces.** Each harness writes its own transcript:

- claude writes session JSONL under its projects home
- codex writes its thread rollout
- dsh writes the session JSONL its persistence plugin appends

If the model echoes a bound value — `echo $GH_TOKEN`, a tool output that prints it, a command line that contains it — that file holds the plaintext. Brokkr cannot mask it at write time, because the harness writes it, not the driver.

Brokkr then **renders** those files. `brokkr transcript`, the TUI's transcript reader and the browser's session view all project the harness transcript through the `brokkr-view` transcript projectors, and none of them masks. So a secret the model saw can be printed on the operator's terminal or served on the loopback UI.

## Why it matters

Decision 0012's layer 5 says a bound value is masked before it reaches "the journal, checkpoints, logs, or the UI". The UI half of that no longer holds for model seats.

The exposure isn't new in kind: before #370, a credential a seat needed could only come from the ambient environment, and the model could read it there too. But #370 makes binding the supported path, so the read surfaces should honour the same masking the journal does.

## Options (the operator rules)

1. **Mask at read time.** The reader runs in the operator's process, which can read the bindings store. It resolves the names the participant's seat declared (from the pinned bundle manifest), and masks projected text with `secret::mask_bytes` / `secret::mask_json` before any surface prints it.
   - Caveat: a value rotated since the run is no longer in the store, so the old value is not masked. Say so on the surface when the store no longer holds a declared name.
2. **Refuse to render.** A participant whose seat declared bindings renders its transcript only with an explicit flag, and says why.
3. Both: mask by default, and say on the surface that masking covers only current store values.

Rewriting the harness's own file is **not** an option: it is the harness's resume record (decision 0030) and not Brokkr's to edit.

## Acceptance

- A fixture transcript for each kind (claude, codex or dsh) that contains a value bound by its seat renders through `brokkr transcript`, the TUI and the browser route with `[secret:NAME]`, never the value. One test per surface.
- The rotated-value case is shown on the surface rather than silently unmasked.
- `docs/guides/secrets.md` says what the read surfaces do.

## Relationship

- #370 (delivery) created the need.
- #352 (one transcript path for claude, codex and dsh) is the natural place to implement it once; if #352 lands first, this goes into its `TurnCollector`.
- #366 (the security model page) should state the resulting guarantee.

Folding a change is the last task: run the archive operation named above,
which moves the change directory under `openspec/changes/archive/` and
folds its deltas into `openspec/specs/`. Folding also records which change
wrote which capability, so every capability the change touched carries a
`## Provenance` list.

After the archive operation, open each capability's
`openspec/specs/<capability>/spec.md` that the change touched and append
exactly one line under a `## Provenance` heading held at the end of the
file:

`- \`<archived-directory-name>\` — folded <YYYY-MM-DD>`

`<archived-directory-name>` is the directory the archive operation
created under `openspec/changes/archive/`; `<YYYY-MM-DD>` is the day it
was folded. Append only: never rewrite, reorder or remove an existing
provenance line, because standing truth accumulates and is not edited into
a different meaning. The line is a pointer, not a summary — it names the
change and nothing else, and the why stays in the change directory.

This realm is a Rust workspace. Production code is Rust under `crates/`; the
Rust-only architecture is recorded by decision 0009. Semantic changes carry a
decision document with status `proposed` because only the operator accepts one.
Intake seats read `README.md` and decisions 0004 and 0005 before framing a
commission, along with the code and history it touches.

The frozen v1 contracts under `contracts/`, the production table at
`policy/phase-machine.json`, `policy/schemas/`, and `reference/` are read-only.
A contract change lands as a new version file beside the old one, never as an
edit. The evaluator corpus under `fixtures/` is also frozen and is never
regenerated, only versioned.

Tests are part of every change. Extend the suite that proves the code, run
`cargo test --workspace`, compile `bundles/self`, and leave formatting, clippy,
and the exact-coverage gate clean before reporting success.

Commit completed work with `git` using the repository's message style. Never
push.

## Release configuration

The release manager prepares the candidate and profile patches; the operator
publishes them. Local validation is preparation work. Remote CI on the final PR
head, publication, channel updates and live-profile verification are handoff
steps, recorded as pending until their remote results exist. Historical
"live from" channel versions and old journal examples are historical facts,
not current-version references to replace.

result.notes: Fixed #380 with option 1 (mask at read time), adapted; the PR should ask the operator to rule. Commit b9087a2c (signed off, not pushed). WHAT: new ui::mask_secrets(read, store) in crates/brokkr-cli/src/ui.rs masks every turn block with secret::mask_bytes against every value in the store beside the journal (ui::store_beside = <journal dir>/secrets.env, where the defaults put .forge/secrets.env next to .forge/forge.db). It then adds the notice 'secrets masked against the store's current values for NAMES; a value rotated or removed since the run is not masked'. If the store cannot be read, it masks nothing and adds 'secrets not masked: <error naming the path>'. A read with no turns, or an absent or empty store, is left unchanged. Wired into all three surfaces: transcript_command (lib.rs), the TUI resolve_subject/resolve_transcript via tui_views(db) (masked before the SourceStamp keeps it), and the browser /api/session/<id> (session_transcript). The session JSON gains a 'notices' member, and ui.html now paints body.notices in place of its truncated-only line; the truncation notice text is identical. docs/guides/secrets.md gains a paragraph on the read surfaces. ASSUMPTION / DEVIATION FROM THE ISSUE: the issue says to resolve the seat's declared names 'from the pinned bundle manifest', but that manifest holds only file digests, and no journal event records declared names or the store path (EffectRequested carries only input_digest; checked engine.rs seat_input/EffectRequested and bundle.rs manifest_for). So the reader masks against every held value, a superset of what the seat bound from that store. It cannot name a specific declared name the store no longer holds; the notice states the rotation and removal caveat on every masked read instead. Also assumed: the store is the one beside the journal, so no new CLI flag was added. A run started with --secrets-file elsewhere, or a realm journal away from its store, is not masked, and the guide says so. TESTS (one per surface, one kind each): tests::the_console_masks_a_bound_value_the_dsh_session_file_holds (TUI, dsh), ui::tests::the_session_drill_masks_a_bound_value_and_says_what_it_covered (browser, claude, plus the 0644 unreadable-store arm and the page paint), and transcript_surfaces::the_command_masks_a_bound_value_and_states_what_a_rotation_leaves (brokkr transcript --json and text, codex, including the rotated value left as written plus the notice). The transcript_surfaces compare() envelope pin moved from three keys to four and now also compares notices. BINDING: mutation 1 replaced mask_bytes(...) with the unmasked bytes; all three tests FAILED (tests.rs:1899, ui/tests.rs:765, transcript_surfaces.rs:842). Mutation 2 dropped the notice push; all three FAILED (tests.rs:1902, ui/tests.rs:771, transcript_surfaces.rs:846). Both were restored. GATES RUN: cargo fmt --all -- --check clean; cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings clean; cargo test -p brokkr-cli --all-features --locked all green (lib 470 passed, transcript_surfaces 7, transcript_command 39, transcript_privacy 9, all other suites ok); git diff --check clean; compile --bundle bundles/self succeeded. No witness digest moved (the witness suites pass unchanged). PENDING: scripts/coverage-exact.sh (the controller runs it; the new branches are exercised by the tests above but not measured here); macOS and CI legs. FOLLOW-UPS: (1) journal the declared secret names and store path at dispatch, so the reader can mask exactly the seat's names and state per-name when the store no longer holds one; (2) #352 TurnCollector would be the single place to host this; (3) #366 should state the guarantee; (4) decide whether an unreadable store should refuse to render rather than show unmasked text with a notice (option 2/3 territory).
